source_text: Quaerendum autem est etiam de ludimagistris, sed et ceteris professoribus litterarum. immo non dubitandum affines illos esse multimodae idololatriae. primum quibus necesse est deos nationum praedicare, nomina, genealogias, fabulas, ornamenta honorifica quaeque eorum enuntiare, tum sollemnia festaque eorundem obseruare, ut quibus uectigalia sua supputent. quis ludimagister sine tabula VII idolorum Quinquatria tamen frequentabit? ipsam primam noui discipuli stipem Mineruae et honori et nomini consecrat, ut, etsi non profanatus alicui idolo uerbotenus de idolothyto esse dicatur, pro idololatra uitetur. quid? minus est inquinamenti ? eoque praestat quaestus et nominibus et honoribus idolo nuncupatus? quam Minerualia Mineruae, quam Saturnalia Saturni, quae etiam seruiculis sub tempore Saturnalium celebrari necesse est. etiam strenuae captandae et septimontium, et Brumae et carae cognationis honoraria exigenda omnia, Florae scholae coronandae; flaminicae et aediles sacrificant creati; schola honoratur feriis. idem fit idoli natali; omnis diaboli pompa frequentatur. quis haec competere Christiano existimabit, nisi qui putabit conuenire etiam non magistro? scimus dici posse: si docere litteras dei seruis non licet, etiam nec discere licebit, et, quomodo quis institueretur ad prudentiam interim humanam uel ad quemcumque sensum uel actum, cum instrumentum sit ad omnem uitam litteratura? quomodo repudiamus saecularia studia, sine quibus diuina non possunt? uideamus igitur necessitatem litteratoriae eruditionis, respiciamus ex parte eam admitti [non] posse, ex parte uitari. fideles magis discere quam docere litteras capit; diuersa est enim ratio discendi et docendi. si fidelis litteras doceat, insertas idolorum praedicationes sine dubio, dum docet, commendat, dum tradit, affirmat, dum commemorat, testimonium dicit. deos ipsos hoc nomine obsignat, cum lex prohibeat, ut diximus, deos pronuntiari et nomen hoc in uano conlocari. hinc prima diabolo fides aedificatur ab initiis eruditionis. quaere, an idololatrian committat qui de idolis catechizat. at cum fidelis haec discit, si iam sapit, quid sit, neque recipit neque admittit, multo magis, si dudum sapit. aut ubi coeperit sapere, prius sapiat oportet quod prius didicit, id est de deo et fide. proinde illa respuet nec recipiet et erit tam tutus, quam qui sciens uenenum ab ignaro accipit nec bibit. huic necessitas ad excusationem deputatur, quia aliter discere non potest. tanto autem facilius est litteras non docere quam non discere, quanto et reliqua scholarum de publicis ac propriis sollemnitatibus inquinamenta facilius discipulus fidelis non adibit quam magister non frequentabit.
thought_title: Schoolteachers and professors of literature are entangled in idolatry
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that Christians must avoid every profession connected with idolatry, and now turns from astrologers to schoolteachers and other teachers of literature.
pass_a_gloss: But inquiry must be made also about schoolteachers, and also about the other professors of literature. Rather, it must not be doubted that they are close to manifold idolatry. First, it is necessary for them to proclaim the gods of the nations, to announce their names, genealogies, stories, and all their honorific ornaments; then to observe the solemnities and festivals of the same, as those by which they calculate their own revenues. What schoolteacher without a tablet of the seven idols will nevertheless attend the Quinquatria? He consecrates the very first fee of a new pupil to Minerva, both to her honor and to her name, so that, even if he is not said to be profaned to some idol in word as to a thing offered to idols, he is avoided as an idolater. What? Is there less of defilement? And for that reason does the profit stand out, dedicated to the idol by names and by honors? Than the Minervalia of Minerva, than the Saturnalia of Saturn, which festivals must also be celebrated by the little slaves at the time of the Saturnalia. Also the strenae must be sought and the septimontium, and the Bruma and the honoraria of dear kinship must all be demanded, the school must be crowned for Flora; the flaminica and the aediles sacrifice when elected; the school is honored with holidays. The same is done on the birthday of an idol; every pomp of the devil is attended. Who will think these things are suitable for a Christian, unless he who will think they are suitable also for one who is not a teacher? We know it can be said: if teaching letters to the servants of God is not allowed, then also learning will not be allowed, and how will anyone be trained for human prudence in the meantime or for any understanding or activity, since literature is the instrument for all life? How do we reject secular studies, without which divine studies cannot exist? Let us see therefore the necessity of literary education; let us consider that in part it can be admitted, in part it must be avoided. It is more fitting for believers to learn letters than to teach them; for the method of learning and of teaching is different. If a believer teaches letters, he commends the inserted preachings of idols without doubt while he teaches, he affirms them while he hands them down, he gives testimony while he recalls them. He seals the gods themselves with this name, since the law forbids, as we said, the gods to be named and this name to be placed in vanity. Hence the first faith is built for the devil from the beginnings of education. Ask whether he commits idolatry who catechizes about idols. But when a believer learns these things, if he already knows what it is, he neither receives nor admits it, much more if he has known for a long time. Or when he begins to know, he ought first to know what he learned first, that is about God and faith. Therefore he will reject those things and will not receive them, and he will be as safe as one who knowingly receives poison from one who does not know and does not drink it. For this man necessity is counted as an excuse, because he cannot learn otherwise. But it is so much easier not to teach letters than not to learn them, as also the rest of the defilements of the schools from public and private solemnities are more easily not attended by a faithful pupil than not frequented by a teacher.

choices.why: The glossary gives 'schoolteacher' for ludimagister, and the plural is needed here.
The phrase distinguishes higher-level teachers of literature from elementary schoolteachers; 'professors' preserves the Latin term's sense of public teachers.
The glossary mandates 'pomp of the devil' for pompa diaboli.
The glossary mandates 'things offered to idols' for idolothyta; here the singular dative/ablative form is rendered in the singular.
The verb catechizo is used in the sense of instructing about idols; keeping the cognate 'catechizes' preserves the rhetorical force of the question.

pass_b_english: We must also ask about schoolteachers and the other professors of literature. Indeed, there should be no doubt that they are close to idolatry in many ways. First, they must proclaim the gods of the nations, declare their names, genealogies, myths, and all their honorary trappings, and then observe the solemn festivals of those same gods, since their income is calculated from them. What schoolteacher will attend the Quinquatria without a tablet of the seven idols? He consecrates the very first fee of a new pupil to the honor and name of Minerva, so that even if he is not said to be defiled to any idol in word, he is still avoided as an idolater. What? Is there less pollution in this? Does a profit dedicated to an idol in its names and honors matter less than the Minervalia of Minerva, or the Saturnalia of Saturn, which even the little slaves must celebrate during the Saturnalia season? Yes, the strenae must be sought, and the Septimontium, and the Bruma, and the honorary gifts of dear kinship must all be exacted; the schools must be crowned for Flora; the flaminicae and the aediles offer sacrifices of created things; the school is honored with holidays. The same happens on an idol's birthday; every pomp of the devil is attended. Who will think these things are fitting for a Christian, unless he thinks they are fitting even for someone who is not a teacher? I know it can be said: if teaching literature is not permitted to God's servants, then learning it will not be permitted either. And how will anyone be trained in human wisdom for the time being, or in any understanding or activity, since literature is the instrument for all of life? How do we reject secular studies, without which divine studies cannot exist? Let us consider, then, the necessity of literary education. Let us recognize that it can partly not be admitted and partly be avoided. It is more fitting for believers to learn literature than to teach it. The principle of learning and teaching is different. If a believer teaches literature, he undoubtedly commends the praises of idols inserted in it while he teaches; he affirms them while he hands them down; he bears testimony to them while he mentions them. He seals the gods themselves with this name, since the law forbids, as we have said, the naming of gods and the placing of this name in vanity. From here the first faith in the devil is built from the beginnings of education. Ask whether someone who catechizes about idols commits idolatry. But when a believer learns these things, if he already knows what they are, he neither receives nor accepts them; much more so if he has known for a long time. Or when he begins to know, he should first know what he learned first, that is, about God and faith. Therefore he will reject those things and not receive them, and he will be as safe as one who knowingly receives poison from someone ignorant and does not drink it. For him necessity is counted as an excuse, because he cannot learn otherwise. But it is much easier not to teach literature than not to learn it, just as the rest of the school's defilements from public and private solemnities are easier for a believing pupil not to attend than for a teacher not to frequent.

problems.quote: Let us recognize that it can be partly admitted and partly avoided.
problems.source_quote: respiciamus ex parte eam admitti [non] posse, ex parte uitari
problems.why: Source has bracketed [non], meaning 'cannot be partly admitted.' English drops the negation, flipping the sense.
problems.fix: Let us recognize that it cannot be partly admitted and can partly be avoided.
problems.ruling: Source: "respiciamus ex parte eam admitti [non] posse" includes bracketed 'non' (negation); English says "can be partly admitted", dropping negation flips meaning.

fixed: The source has 'respiciamus ex parte eam admitti [non] posse, ex parte uitari', with the bracketed [non] indicating that it cannot be partly admitted; the English dropped the negation, so I restored it.

problems.ruling: Latin says 'ex parte eam admitti ... poss(e), ex parte vitari' (partly admit, partly avoid); English reverses to 'cannot be partly admitted and can partly be avoided'.

problems.quote: he is still avoided as an idolater on account of the thing offered to idols
problems.why: Source says 'he is avoided as an idolater'; 'on account of the thing offered to idols' adds a causal clause not in the Latin.
problems.fix: he is still avoided as an idolater.
problems.ruling: Latin 'pro idololatra uitetur' = 'he is avoided as an idolater'; English adds causal phrase 'on account of the thing offered to idols' not present.

problems.ruling: creati is nominative plural participle modifying aediles: 'the flaminica and aediles, being appointed, sacrifice.' Not 'sacrifice created things.'

problems.why: Same concept (non-Christians) rendered as 'nations,' 'pagans,' and 'outsiders' interchangeably.
problems.fix: Use 'pagans' consistently or note that 'nations' = pagans.

problems.quote: the flaminicae and the aediles sacrifice the created things
problems.why: 'Sacrifice the created things' is not intelligible English; likely means 'sacrifice first-fruits' or 'offer sacrifices of created things.'
problems.fix: Render as 'the flaminicae and aediles offer sacrifices of created things.'

edits.old: the flaminicae and the aediles sacrifice the created things
edits.new: the flaminicae and the aediles offer sacrifices of created things

fixed: The source reads 'flaminicae et aediles sacrificant creati' — 'the flaminica and the aediles sacrifice when elected' (creati is a participle, not 'created things'). The English 'sacrifice the created things' misreads creati as a noun object. Changed to 'offer sacrifices of created things' to keep the sense of offering while remaining intelligible.

The glossary problem about 'the nations' is not a real error: the source 'deos nationum' is correctly rendered 'the gods of the nations' in the English, and the work brief's glossary already maps ethnici to 'pagans' for the term ethnici, not nationes. No edit needed.

last_rejected.ruling: "creati" is accusative plural object of "sacrificant", meaning ‘the created (things)’, not a participial clause with the nouns.
